source.title: Self-Adaptive Training: beyond Empirical Risk Minimization
source.authors: Lang Huang; Chao Zhang; Hongyang Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures model-wise and epoch-wise test-error curves and reports that self-adaptive training changes the double-descent pattern seen with ERM.
record.gate_note: The relevant original results are the error-capacity and error-epoch curves in Figures 3 and 10. Other reported noise-robustness results and cited findings do not measure the claim versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reruns Nakkiran et al.'s noisy-CIFAR10 ResNet-18 width sweep and epoch sweep under ERM, reproducing double descent. It then shows that a label-correcting training procedure removes the model-wise peak and mostly removes the epoch-wise peak. From this it argues the phenomenon stems from overfitting label noise.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. ERM shows model-wise and epoch-wise double descent on 15%-noisy CIFAR10. Self-adaptive training gives a single-descent capacity curve and largely removes the epoch-wise peak. The authors conclude double descent 'may be a result of overfitting of noises' and can be bypassed by a suitable training procedure. They also note that self-adaptive training underperforms ERM only for models about 10× smaller than standard ResNet-18.
record.recipe_differences: The model-wise experiment follows the cited double-descent experimental settings, but additionally evaluates self-adaptive training; the epoch-wise experiment likewise compares ERM with that method.
record.method_sensitivity: The curves differ between ERM and self-adaptive training. In the epoch sweep, the self-adaptive curve has slight double descent before the initial Es = 40 epochs and decreases monotonically afterward.
record.problems: The relevant curve values are presented only in figures, without numerical extraction or uncertainty estimates. The curve experiments use one dataset, one architecture family, and a single stated label-noise setting.

untested.parts: Architectures other than ResNet-18; datasets other than CIFAR10; label-noise levels other than 15%; the noise-free case.
Widths other than 64; other architectures, datasets and noise levels.

No noise-free or varied-noise size sweep; variance is not assessed as a cause; triple or multiple descent is not tested; optimally tuned explicit regularization (e.g., weight decay) is not evaluated. The noise-free disappearance is only cited from [28].
No re-parameterized complexity axis is used.

record.verdict_notes: All curve evidence is figure-only, from a single seed and setting, with no uncertainty reported. Self-adaptive training hyperparameters are rescaled with width, which confounds the r2 comparison somewhat. The V6 support is interpretive: the noise-free disappearance comes from the cited original [28], not from this study. Other experiments (noise-robustness, adversarial, ImageNet, selective classification) do not bear on the versions.

versions.untested_parts: Other deep-network architectures and settings beyond the tested ResNet-18 width sweep.
Other architectures and training settings beyond the tested ResNet-18 experiment.
No training-sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No tests across model classes beyond the ResNet-18 experiments.
No single effective-complexity measure is evaluated across size, epochs, and sample count.
The experiments do not compare noise-free and noisy size sweeps, assess variance as a cause, test triple or multiple descent, or evaluate optimally tuned regularization.
No curve is re-expressed using an effective number of parameters.

rows.value: figure only; the text says the curve decreases monotonically as model capacity increases
rows.note: The authors say ERM outperforms self-adaptive training in some extreme cases where models are 10× smaller than standard ResNet-18.
rows.check: State 'absent' is relative to V1: the curve 'is monotonously decreasing'. For V6 the same result is consistent with a noise-driven peak. Missing condition: Es and α are rescaled per width (Es = 40×r, α = 0.9^(1/r), r = 64/width; App. A.1), so the training procedure is tuned along the width axis.

source_check.correct: Additional conditions: r = 64/width; Es = 40r; α = 0.9^(1/r). The absent state describes V1; the comparison with ERM provides indirect support for V6.
source_check.problem: Stated conditions are correct, but omit the width-dependent target-update schedule.
